plan.fit_summary: Tier A fit: DACHSER is headquartered in Kempten, Germany [2] and runs a Food Logistics business line that grew 10.1 percent to over EUR 1.8 billion in 2025 [6], so temperature monitoring and audit reporting are core to its operations.

who.why: Owns the business line that grew 10.1 percent to over EUR 1.8 billion in 2025 [6], where temperature-controlled transport and warehousing sit.
DACHSER operates a compliance reporting system [3], so audit-ready temperature documentation falls in this remit.

plan.hook: DACHSER increased its Food Logistics revenue by 10.1 percent to over EUR 1.8 billion in 2025 [6]. That growth means more customers asking for temperature proof in audits — ColdTrace automates exactly that documentation.
plan.channel: Phone call to the Kempten headquarters [2], asking for the Head of Food Logistics. DACHSER is based in Germany, where UWG § 7 (2) no. 2 requires prior express consent for electronic mail, also in B2B, and courts treat social-network messages as electronic mail — so no cold email or LinkedIn/XING DM as first touch. A B2B call needs at least presumed consent, which is plausible here because temperature monitoring in food logistics is directly tied to the recipient's trade; a letter is the fallback. Not legal advice.
avoid: Do not use cold email or LinkedIn/XING DM as the first touch — German law requires prior express consent for electronic mail, also in B2B.
Do not claim DACHSER has temperature-monitoring gaps or audit problems — no source supports that.
Do not name or guess an individual contact; address roles only.
Do not quote the '427 locations' figure — it does not appear word for word in the provided source text.
questions: How do you currently produce temperature documentation for customer audits across your food logistics warehouses — manually or from an automated system?
